caption: Size of physical and instrumental effects, as the magnitude |Δλ| (sign and range in the third column). Velocity-like effects are converted at λ = 5000 Å (Δλ = λ·v/c, 1 mÅ ≙ 59.96 m/s); effects tied to a line or band (isotope shifts, hyperfine and fine structure, telluric pressure shifts, UVES) are given at that wavelength, stated in the λ column (for telluric molecules the median λ of the selected lines, which span O₂ 0.58–1.30 µm, CO₂ 1.20–2.17 µm, H₂O 0.44–2.50 µm, CH₄ 1.13–2.50 µm). Telluric pressure shifts are medians of δair·peff over the selected lines, with peff the S·u-weighted pressure along a vertical sea-level path in the US Standard atmosphere; they neglect line mixing, speed dependence and the temperature dependence of δ. Air-state sensitivities use the full Ciddor (1996) model at λvac = 5000 Å. “derived” marks values computed for this page (DE440s, IAU 2015 nominal constants, HITRAN2024 parameters, NIST Handbook/ASD comparison); the derivations are in data/notes/precision_rationale.md and relativity_cosmology.md. Rows below ≈ 1 mÅ are kept because they decide what the barycentric correction (§7.4) must contain.
